alt: A grid of the six relational operators applied to 7 and 7, 5 and 9, and 9 and 5. For equal values only =, ≤ and ≥ are True. For 5 and 9, ≠, < and ≤ are True; for 9 and 5, ≠, > and ≥ are True.
caption: Each comparison gives True or False; the equal case is where the operators differ most.

alt: Six phrases and their conditions on a number line around 50. "At least 50" is mark ≥ 50 and "no more than 50" is mark ≤ 50, both including 50. "More than 50" is mark > 50 and "less than 50" is mark < 50, both excluding 50. "Exactly 50" is mark = 50 and "anything except 50" is mark ≠ 50.
caption: The boundary words decide whether 50 itself is included.

alt: Number lines split at 10. count < 10 covers everything below 10 and its opposite count ≥ 10 covers 10 and above; count ≤ 10 and count > 10 split the line the other way. count = 10 is the opposite of count ≠ 10. So WHILE count < 10 becomes UNTIL count ≥ 10, not UNTIL count > 10.
caption: Opposites split the line with no gap: < with ≥, > with ≤, = with ≠.

alt: The strings "yes" and "Yes" are compared character by character; the first characters differ in case, so "yes" = "Yes" is False, while "yes" = "yes" is True. A menu expecting "Y" will not accept "y" unless the condition allows both, and "12" must be converted before it is compared with the integer 12.
caption: String comparison checks every character, including case.

after: ## Worked example: choosing a band from a value
alt: An IF … ELSE IF chain puts times under 20 in Fast, times from 20 up to under 30 in Steady, and 30 or more in Starter. On a number line the boundaries are at 20 and 30. A trace of 18, 20, 29 and 30 gives Fast, Steady, Steady and Starter; 20 and 30 are the boundary values.
caption: Tests run in order, and boundary values reveal whether < or ≤ was the right choice.

alt: Two WHILE loops start count at 0 and output it before adding 1. With WHILE count < 5 the output is 0, 1, 2, 3, 4: five values. With WHILE count ≤ 5 the output is 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5: six values.
caption: Changing < to ≤ adds one more pass of the loop.
